paras: In August 1910 the police of Beatrice, Nebraska, ordered eight Black people out of the city after arresting four of them on vagrancy and vice charges. The eight left by train for Lincoln, and the authorities said they would keep similar newcomers out. The Beatrice Daily Express reported it under the headline "Population Decreasing," and a state-news column carried it elsewhere in Nebraska.

On Sunday, August 14, local officers arrested two Black men, one charged with vagrancy and the other with soliciting business for a disorderly house. The next day the Express reported that the two were in the city jail awaiting trial and that "the colored men will be given the privilege of working on the street or leaving town."

Late on the afternoon of August 15 the two men were heard in police court before Judge Ellis, who gave one ten days in jail and fined the other $25 and costs. That evening Officers Clyde Reed and Hy Bales arrested two more Black people, a man and a woman. According to the Express, the four, "with a number of their friends, eight in all," were then ordered out of town by the police and took the early morning Burlington for Lincoln; none of the eight was named.

The Express wrote that "very undesirable characters" had come to Beatrice from Lincoln in the past few days and that others would be ordered "to make themselves scarce and keep out of the corporate limits."

The Express treated the matter as police news, first in a city brevity and then in a front-page item headed "Population Decreasing." Nine days later the Loup City Northwestern ran a one-paragraph version in its state-news column, reporting that "a number of negroes" had been ordered out.
Neither paper stated a racial reason for the order, but both identified the people only by race, and no Black-press coverage was found.

The accounts agree that three men and a woman were arrested but differ on the charges: the Express named vagrancy and soliciting for a disorderly house, the Loup City brief vagrancy and disorderly conduct.

reader.title: Ordering out of Black visitors from Beatrice, Nebraska
bases: Beatrice police ordered eight Black people, four of them just arrested on vagrancy and vice charges, out of the city, and they left by train for Lincoln (A2, A4).

Every account comes from Beatrice reporting: two items in the Beatrice Daily Express (A1, A2) and a state-news brief in the Loup City Northwestern (A4) whose Beatrice items on the same page appear to rework the Express, so no independent report was found.

accounts.label: Beatrice Daily Express (local police news)
accounts.gist: Four Black people arrested on vagrancy and vice charges and four friends were ordered out of town by the police and left on the early morning Burlington for Lincoln; more arrivals from Lincoln would be ordered out.

accounts.label: State-news brief
accounts.gist: A number of Black people in Beatrice were ordered out of town after three men were arrested for vagrancy and a woman for disorderly conduct; the city would try to keep such people out.

framing.detail: The Express headlined the expulsion 'Population Decreasing' and described the people from Lincoln as 'very undesirable characters' who would be told to 'make themselves scarce.'
The Loup City Northwestern ran the item as one line of state news, repeating the authorities' plan to keep 'characters of this class' out.

versions.value: One of the first two men charged with vagrancy and the other with soliciting for a disorderly house; charges for the second pair not stated
Three men charged with vagrancy and the woman with disorderly conduct

conflicts.note: Both versions agree on three men and one woman arrested; the local Express is the more detailed and nearer source on the charges.

record_check.dossier: Arrests on August 14 and 15; the order to leave followed the evening arrests of August 15 and the eight left on the early morning train, apparently August 16.
No names are given; eight people, four of them arrested (three men and one woman).
Vagrancy and soliciting for a disorderly house (or disorderly conduct) for the four arrested; none stated for the friends.
The Beatrice police (Officers Clyde Reed and Hy Bales named for the arrests).
Three relevant white-press items: two in the Beatrice Daily Express (August 15 and 16) and one in the Loup City Northwestern.

info: Two Black men were arrested Sunday, August 14; two more were arrested the evening of Monday, August 15; the eight left Beatrice by the early morning train, apparently on August 16.
Eight unnamed Black people: four arrested (two men on Sunday, then a man and a woman) and 'a number of their friends'; the Loup City brief counts three men and one woman arrested.
Vagrancy and soliciting for a disorderly house (Express); vagrancy for three men and disorderly conduct for the woman (Loup City brief). The friends were not reported as charged.
The Beatrice police; Officers Clyde Reed and Hy Bales made the second arrests, and Judge Ellis heard the first two cases in police court.
